nodes.body: <<FILL role=success words=95 beats='the name in the cornet case belongs to a grandmother in the next street who played until she was nineteen and has not said so out loud in fifty years, and she takes the case back and then, after a fortnight, brings it to a practice'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=95 beats='two copies, one signature each, a list of eleven items and a date, done on a Tuesday evening in the school hall with the residents watching; it is the least dramatic twenty minutes of the whole fortnight and the only reason none of it comes apart later'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=95 beats='a minute book from 1934, four hundred photographs, a run of programmes and one card headed THE ROUNDS, accessioned, numbered and on a shelf with a date stamp on the back of every sheet; Aisha puts the whistle photograph in the case by the door'>>

<<FILL role=discovery words=95 beats='Deniz leaves the plate uncovered and moves the menu board a foot to the left, and for about a month people come into the chip shop to look at a piece of brass and buy chips while they are there; then they stop, and the plate stays'>>

ending.title: The Plate Under the Menu Board

nodes.body: <<FILL role=setback words=95 beats='the story runs on Friday under a photograph of an empty store and a skip, and it is a good piece of writing about something that has already happened; four people write in to say they would have helped if anybody had asked them on Tuesday'>>

<<FILL role=success words=95 beats='eleven players, one borrowed drum, a photocopied map and six brass plates, and the band stops at all six stops in the cold and plays badly at each one; more people follow it round than anybody expected and half of them are under twelve'>>

<<FILL role=success words=95 beats='forty people walk the route on a Saturday in October behind a man of eighty-four who stops at each plate and says what stood there, and at the weighbridge, where there is no plate at all, everybody stands in a car park and listens anyway'>>

<<FILL role=success words=95 beats='five plates go back onto five walls with the right screws and the sixth is cut new in brass by a man in the industrial estate who will not take money for it, and it goes onto the car park wall in the rectangle that has been waiting twenty-eight years'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=95 beats='the whistle goes back into the case with the card folded into eighths beside it and lives on a shelf, played badly about once a week, and it is the only object in the story that ends up exactly where it started and means something completely different'>>

ending.title: Six Plates Back on Six Walls

nodes.body: <<FILL role=completion words=95 beats='instruments to the school, paper to the library, photograph to the almshouses, plates to the walls and the card to the archive with a note saying who found it; it takes three weeks of small dull errands and nothing is left in a bag under anybody bed'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=95 beats='the store comes out onto the grass, gets listed, photographed and divided into keep and skip in front of two men who are being paid by the hour and are surprisingly interested, and the room underneath the bandstand ends the week swept, dry and empty'>>

<<FILL role=setback words=95 beats='the skip leaves the park at nine on Friday morning with a bass drum and four cases in it, and there is a photograph of it going, taken from the gate, that the Gazette will not print because there is nothing to say about it'>>

<<FILL role=setback words=95 beats='three separate adults would have stopped it and none of them were told, because asking felt like a bigger thing on Wednesday than it turned out to be on the following Monday when all three said so in turn'>>

<<FILL role=setback words=95 beats='the last order is wrong, the wheels go back to zero, and the trail that ran from a shoebox in Perch Lane through six walls and sixty years ends at a steel door in a cold park with a lorry booked for the morning'>>

ending.title: The Trail Ends at a Steel Door
